articles.title: Malaysia's king warns against challenging a pardon allowing former prime minister Najib Razak to serve his final two years at home, after the transfer was delayed despite his party paying a $12 million fine
articles.summary: Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim has warned that any attempt to challenge his order allowing former Prime Minister Najib Razak to serve the remaining two
articles.body: Malaysia’s King Sultan Ibrahim has warned that any attempt to challenge his order allowing former Prime Minister Najib Razak to serve the remaining two years of his sentence under house arrest could amount to defying his decree. The warning came a day after authorities delayed Najib’s transfer from prison, despite his party paying a 50-million-ringgit fine, about $12 million, to meet a condition of the royal pardon issued in September, as per reports by Reuters, Al Jazeera and South China Morning Post (SCMP).Najib, who has been in jail since 2022 after being convicted of corruption and money laundering in a case linked to the 1Malaysia Development Berhad scandal, was due to be transferred home on Friday. The attorney-general’s office said questions had arisen over the legal interpretation of the royal pardon and a court order allowing Najib to leave jail, prompting the suspension. Read more details about it, as per the reports, here:What the king saidIn a statement issued by the national palace, Sultan Ibrahim said his pardon order was clear, explicit and without any ambiguity. He noted that the attorney-general and the federal territories minister had attended the pardons board meeting at which the order was issued.The king said there should be no confusion over its interpretation, nor should there be prolonged uncertainty over the implementation of the decision that has been granted. He warned that any attempt to challenge the order could amount to defying his decree.The king’s position carries weight in Malaysia, where the monarch and the country’s other sultans are held in deep respect. Negative remarks about royalty can be prosecuted under the colonial-era Sedition Act.What the attorney-general saidThe attorney-general’s chambers responded to accusations from Najib’s lawyers of executive overreach, saying it was only seeking legal clarity. The office said it had never disputed, set aside or intended to suspend the conditional pardon order granted by the king.The AGC said the issue should be referred immediately to the court for a clear determination and directions. That response suggests the delay was not a rejection of the pardon, but an attempt to resolve a legal question before Najib is moved.The chambers did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside office hours, according to Reuters.How the pardon came aboutNajib’s party, the United Malays National Organisation, used crowdfunding to cover the 50-million-ringgit fine, since his bank accounts have been frozen. The fine was a condition of the royal pardon issued by King Sultan Ibrahim in September.The pardon allows Najib to serve the remaining two years of his sentence at home, rather than in prison. His lawyer, Farhan Shafee, told reporters on Friday that he had been given the order and was delivering it to Kajang prison.Najib has been in jail since 2022 after being found guilty of corruption and embezzlement of billions of dollars connected to 1Malaysia Development Berhad, a state investment fund he co-founded while in power from 2009 to 2018. He has repeatedly denied all wrongdoing, the reports said.What the 1MDB case involvedInvestigators say about $4.5 billion was stolen from the 1MDB state fund, with more than $1 billion linked to Najib. The scandal has been one of the largest financial fraud cases in modern history.Najib was also convicted in a separate 1MDB trial in Malaysia, where he was sentenced to 15 years in prison and a $2.5 billion fine for money laundering and abuse of power. He has appealed that case, and his lawyers requested that the jail term and fines be halted, citing poor health and his inability to pay.A judge rejected that request in September, saying the gravity of the offence was a more important public interest consideration. Najib is due to return to jail to serve out that sentence once his house arrest ends in 2028, though it is unclear at this stage whether that will happen.Why the delay mattersThe delay in Najib’s transfer has created a political stir in Malaysia, according to Al Jazeera’s Rob McBride, who reported from Kuala Lumpur. He said the decision could impact the political scene, with questions being asked about how current politics have influenced the pardon.Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim has publicly raised concerns about the pardon in his capacity as the country’s anticorruption figurehead. There has also been speculation that he may have helped the pardon go through behind the scenes due to pressure from Najib’s party.The king’s warning adds another layer to the situation. By framing any challenge to the order as a potential act of defiance, Sultan Ibrahim has made clear that he expects the pardon to be implemented as issued.What happens nextThe attorney-general’s office has asked for the matter to be referred to the court for a clear determination and directions. That means the legal question over the pardon’s interpretation will likely be resolved through the judiciary rather than through further political negotiation.For Najib, the immediate question is whether he will be transferred to house arrest as planned. The king’s statement suggests he expects that to happen, but the attorney-general’s request for legal clarity means the timeline is not yet certain.The case is a reminder of how royal pardons, constitutional powers and political pressure can intersect in Malaysia’s system. articles.title: A Florida husband went to his estranged wife's condo asking about his Ferrari; video of that visit alone did not justify a domestic violence order, but an appeals court upheld her protection based on earlier incidents
articles.summary: A Florida appeals court has upheld a domestic violence protection order against a husband who visited his estranged wife's condo asking about his Ferrari.
articles.body: A Florida appeals court has upheld a domestic violence protection order against a husband who visited his estranged wife's condo asking about his Ferrari. The November 6 ruling involved Gerald Buchheit and his wife, Cara Siciliano, who were going through a divorce. The court found that a video of the December 2024 visit did not show domestic violence. However, it upheld the protection order because Siciliano had described three earlier incidents in which Buchheit allegedly physically assaulted her.According to case details available on Justia, the couple had been separated since 2022. Buchheit lived in Buffalo, New York, while Siciliano lived in Fort Myers, Florida. In December 2024, he went to her condo without informing her in advance. He said he wanted to collect his mail, leave some gifts he had bought in Italy and ask about his Ferrari, which he could not find in the garage.Siciliano said Buchheit arrived at around 7 am while she and her 17-year-old daughter were at home. She alleged that he entered her bedroom, shouted at her and recorded her while demanding to know where his Ferrari was. She also claimed that he followed her around the condo and threatened to return whenever he wanted.Siciliano subsequently approached the court for protection, saying she feared for her safety. Buchheit denied her allegations and argued that the video of the visit showed that he had not threatened or chased her.The trial court granted Siciliano's request after hearing about the couple's earlier history. Buchheit challenged the decision, but the Sixth District Court of Appeal of Florida upheld the protection order.What happened during the Ferrari argument?During the hearing, both Buchheit and Siciliano gave different accounts of the visit. Buchheit said he had gone to the condo to collect his mail and leave gifts for his wife. He also wanted to know where his Ferrari was.He denied kicking open her bedroom door, seeing her naked or chasing her through the condo. He said Siciliano started shouting at him to leave. He also explained that he recorded the interaction because he did not want to be falsely accused of wrongdoing.The court examined the 62-second video of the visit. It showed Buchheit standing outside a closed door and calmly asking, "where's the Ferrari?" Siciliano's daughter responded, "and why are you here?" Buchheit replied, "I bought this house. That's why I'm here."The recording then showed Siciliano standing in the living room in a bathrobe, on the other side of a large couch. She asked him to leave while dialling on her phone.Buchheit slowly walked towards her bedroom. Siciliano closed the bedroom door as he approached. He appeared to open it slightly, but she shut it again. He then walked towards the condo's exit, and the video ended.The appeals court said the recording did not show Buchheit shouting, chasing Siciliano, behaving aggressively or making threats. It agreed that the December 2024 visit alone could not justify the final protection order. However, the court also considered Siciliano's testimony about earlier incidents of physical violence.Wife described three earlier assaultsSiciliano told the court about four incidents dating from 2016 to 2023. She said Buchheit had slammed her into a bedroom door in January 2023, splitting it in half. She said this happened after she had undergone breast cancer surgery.Buchheit objected to this incident because it had not been mentioned in her original petition. The appeals court agreed that the trial court should not have considered it because he had not been given prior notice of the allegation.However, Siciliano also described three other incidents that Buchheit did not object to during the hearing. She said that in June 2016, he shattered a wine glass and cut the back of her leg. In March 2020, she alleged that he choked her while drunk, attacked her and smashed her phone, leaving bruises on her arm. In February 2022, she said he punched her repeatedly in the back at Mar-a-Lago.Buchheit disputed these accounts. He said the wine glass had fallen and caused the cut. He claimed that the bruises in 2020 happened while he was trying to stop Siciliano from hitting him. He also denied the alleged assault at Mar-a-Lago.Siciliano said she had not contacted the police or sought protection after these incidents. She explained that Buchheit had several residences, moved around frequently and had filed for divorce. Although they jointly owned the Fort Myers condo, he did not live there or keep his belongings there.She also told the court that his behaviour had worsened after he was involved in a plane crash earlier in 2024. According to her, he had started drinking more frequently. She said all the earlier incidents of violence had happened when he was drinking.Court upheld the protection orderThe appeals court said the three earlier incidents were enough to support the protection order. Under Florida law, a person can obtain a final domestic violence injunction if they have been a victim of domestic violence or have reasonable grounds to fear further violence.The court said the law does not set a time limit on how far back judges can consider incidents of domestic violence. It also requires courts to examine the history between the two people, including physical abuse and threats, while assessing the risk of future violence.The judges said the earlier incidents showed that Siciliano had been a victim of domestic violence. They also considered her fear following Buchheit's unannounced visit.She had told the court that he was drinking more after the plane crash, that alcohol had been linked to his earlier violence and that the couple were going through a divorce. The court said these circumstances helped explain her fear when he appeared at her home without warning.Buchheit had argued that the earlier incidents were too old to justify a new protection order. However, he raised this argument for the first time in his motion for rehearing, after the trial court had already issued its decision. The appeals court said he had raised the issue too late and could not challenge it at this stage.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Iran distributes iodine pills near nuclear sites as Trump weighs fresh strikes: Report
articles.summary: Iran has started distributing iodine tablets to people living near its nuclear facilities amid growing fears of a possible fresh US military strike,
articles.body: Iran has started distributing iodine tablets to people living near its nuclear facilities amid growing fears of a possible fresh US military strike, according to media reports. The move comes as US President Donald Trump weighs whether to resume military operations against Tehran and US forces prepare for a possible escalation.An Iranian health ministry official confirmed the distribution in comments cited by the Al Jazeera."Yes, we are distributing iodine," the official was quoted as saying. "Trump can no longer be trusted. He may go through with this crime, " as per Al Jazeera.The official said Iran routinely provides the preventive medication to residents living within a 2-3 km radius of nuclear installations when military tensions rise.Iodine tablets are used to protect the thyroid gland from absorbing radioactive iodine in the event of a nuclear incident. Their distribution does not, by itself, indicate that a radiation emergency is imminent.US weighs fresh military actionThe latest reports also point to growing military preparations in Washington. An Iranian political journalist told Al Jazeera that state officials were informed during a recent briefing that a possible US strike on the heavily fortified Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site was being seriously considered.Trump met his national security team on Thursday to discuss whether military operations against Iran should resume, Fox News reported, citing senior US officials. The meetings reportedly took place at the White House on Wednesday and Thursday.Fox News also highlighted that November 9 would bring a new moon in the Middle East, leaving little or no moonlight. Such conditions can be advantageous for military operations, although there has been no confirmation that any strike has been scheduled.Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said Washington would soon "make a decision" on whether to resume the war.He questioned whether the US should launch further attacks to ensure Iran's nuclear programme was permanently dismantled and "it will never happen again"."I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You'll know soon enough," Trump said.Meanwhile, a US official told media outlets that the US Central Command was finalising preparations for a possible resumption of major military operations against Iran. However, Washington had not yet issued formal orders to proceed.Iraq warns against using its territory for strikesAmid the rising tensions, Iraqi prime minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi spoke to Trump over the phone on Thursday and made clear that Iraq would not allow its territory to be used as a launchpad for attacks on neighbouring countries.A statement issued by the prime minister's office on X reiterated Baghdad's position."Mr. Prime Minister affirmed Iraq's position calling for respect for the sovereignty of states, non-use of its territories as a launchpad for aggression against neighbouring countries."Iraq's warning comes as the possibility of renewed US military action against Iran raises concerns about a wider regional escalation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Saudi strike killed 22 people, mostly women & kids, near Yemen's capital: Houthi official
articles.summary: At least 22 people were killed and 30 others wounded in airstrikes on a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday, according to the Houthi-run
articles.body: At least 22 people were killed and 30 others wounded in airstrikes on a village near Yemen's capital, Sanaa, on Saturday, according to the Houthi-run health ministry. The latest attack takes the reported death toll from two separate strikes in the country over two days to at least 52, with 38 others injured.Most of those killed or wounded in Saturday's attack on al-Shariya village were women and children, said Anees Alasbahi, a spokesperson for the Houthi-run Health Ministry. He accused Saudi Arabia of carrying out the strikes. Riyadh had not issued an immediate response to the allegation.The latest attack came a day after a deadly strike on al-Hadara market in al-Waziyah district of southwestern Yemen's Taiz province. Houthi officials said at least 30 people were killed and eight others wounded in that incident.The Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces have blamed each other for the market attack, with neither side's claims independently verified by The Associated Press.Market turns into deadly strike zoneThe earlier attack took place at around 7 am on Friday, according to Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree. He said three airstrikes hit al-Hadara market and accused Saudi Arabia of carrying them out.Saree claimed the warplanes had taken off from the Khamis Mushait air base and left Taiz province around 8 am. However, he did not provide evidence to support the allegation.Authorities aligned with Yemen's Saudi-backed government blamed the Houthis for the attack and denied that any airstrikes had taken place in the area.The provincial media office acknowledged that the busy market had been attacked and that there were casualties, but did not provide a death toll. It also accused the Houthis of carrying out "indiscriminate Houthi missile attacks", including the use of ballistic missiles.Footage aired by Houthi-run Al-Masirah television showed smoke rising from the market, with damaged buildings, destroyed vehicles, scattered fruit boxes and debris.Fighting intensifies around TaizThe two deadly incidents come amid renewed fighting between the Houthis and forces backing Yemen's internationally recognised government.Taiz remains a strategically important province. The Houthis control much of the surrounding territory and have besieged the provincial capital, which remains under government control.The rebels stepped up their advance towards Taiz in September after capturing the port city of Mokha, around 130 km away. The port is strategically important because of its location near the Red Sea shipping route.The Houthis have also carried out deadly attacks on government forces. Last month, a ballistic missile strike by the group on a military camp in the southern province of Shabwa killed at least 75 soldiers and wounded around 200 recruits. The rebels acknowledged carrying out that attack.In September, the Houthis accused Saudi Arabia of striking a prison in Hazm, the provincial capital of al-Jawf. At least 23 people were killed after the prison collapsed during coalition airstrikes in the area.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Poor Biharis don't know anything': Congress UP in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam targets BJP chief Nitin Nabin
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam on Saturday hit out at BJP national president Nitin Nabin over his \"toolkit\" remark
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Congress' Uttar Pradesh in-charge Rajendra Pal Gautam on Saturday hit out at BJP national president Nitin Nabin over his "toolkit" remark targeting Congress MP Rahul Gandhi.In a swipe at Nabin, Gautam remarked that "poor Biharis" could only read from scripts handed to them. Bihar is the BJP chief's home state.“These poor Biharis do not know anything. They simply read out scripts handed to them,” he told news agency IANS.The Congress leader also claimed that BJP leaders were "incapable" of acting independently and accused them of misappropriating donations made in the name of Lord Ram. He was referring to the alleged theft of offerings at the Ram Temple in Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh.“They (BJP leaders) are incapable of doing anything on their own. They are people who steal offerings. They have betrayed people's faith. They came to power in the name of Lord Ram and then stole offerings made in his name. So, whose interests do they serve? We do not take them seriously,” he said.Gautam's remarks came after Nabin, also in an interview with IANS, accused Rahul Gandhi of being used as an "instrument to destabilise the country." The BJP chief alleged that the Lok Sabha leader of the opposition was acting as part of a "foreign toolkit".Nabin cited remarks by Jharkhand minister and Congress leader Irfan Ansari, who claimed that Rahul Gandhi had "complete control" over the "remote button" and could mobilise "40 lakh people" to protest against the Narendra Modi government, similar to the student- and youth-led demonstrations that led to the fall of governments in neighbouring Nepal and Bangladesh.“You saw how a Congress minister (Ansari) said that Rahul Gandhi has complete control over the remote button and that, whenever he wants, 40 lakh people are ready to create anarchy in the country. I believe this clearly confirms what we have been saying from the beginning — that Rahul Gandhi is being used as a toolkit to destabilise the country and create anarchy,” Nabin said.However, he asserted that India’s democratic foundations remain strong and that the country would give a “fitting response” to those who tried to spread “chaos.”“The democratic roots of this nation are strong. If people think they can destabilise India or spread chaos, they are mistaken. This country will give a fitting response to individuals with such anarchic and Maoist-leaning mindsets," Nabin added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: How much does the British Royal Family cost taxpayers? King Charles' Sovereign Grant rises to £137.9 million as new bill proposes reduction; Prince William's £1.2 billion Duchy wealth also revealed
articles.summary: How much does the British Royal Family cost British taxpayers, and how wealthy are King Charles III and Prince William?
articles.body: How much does the British Royal Family cost British taxpayers, and how wealthy are King Charles III and Prince William? A new UK Parliament briefing on royal finances has revealed how public money supports the monarchy, while also explaining the income generated by historic royal estates and the tax arrangements followed by senior members of the family. The Sovereign Grant, which funds the King's official duties, stands at £137.9 million for 2026/27. However, the government has proposed reducing it to £99.9 million in 2027/28 following the completion of the Buckingham Palace refurbishment.Meanwhile, a report by The Mirror has drawn attention to Prince William's financial position, including the £1.2 billion valuation of the Duchy of Cornwall and his reported £21.6 million income in 2025-26. King Charles, meanwhile, has an estimated personal fortune of £640 million, according to the Sunday Times Rich List. Here's how the Royal Family earns its money, pays taxes and uses public funding.How much does the British Royal Family receive from taxpayers?The Sovereign Grant was introduced in 2012/13 under the Sovereign Grant Act 2011, replacing earlier sources of royal funding, including the Civil List. According to the House of Commons Library briefing, the grant has reached £137.9 million for 2026/27.The money covers the maintenance of occupied royal palaces, official travel undertaken by the King and members of the Royal Family representing him, and the salaries and employment costs of Royal Household staff. It also supports official duties and events. The grant is intended for the monarchy's public responsibilities, not the King's private expenditure.Its calculation is linked to, but not directly derived from, profits generated by the Crown Estate. The amount is reviewed every five years, with the latest review beginning in 2026.Why is King Charles' Sovereign Grant set to fall to £99.9 million?The government has introduced the Sovereign Grant Bill 2026-27, which proposes reducing the grant after the completion of Buckingham Palace's extensive refurbishment programme.Subject to the legislation, the funding will fall to £99.9 million in 2027/28. However, the proposed amount would still be 65% higher in real terms than the funding received in 2016/17, before the palace's major reservicing programme began.The bill also proposes a mechanism for future reductions to prevent what the government describes as 'inappropriately high funding'.Is Prince William richer than King Charles? Inside the £1.2 billion Duchy of CornwallAccording to The Mirror, the Duchy of Cornwall, which provides income to the heir to the throne, is valued at approximately £1.2 billion. Prince William became the 25th Duke of Cornwall after Queen Elizabeth II's death and King Charles' accession in September 2022. He is entitled to the estate's annual profits as the Prince of Wales.The estate covers approximately 51,800 hectares across 19 counties. Its accounts show that William received £21.6 million in private income during 2025-26. In comparison, King Charles' personal fortune has been estimated at £640 million by the Sunday Times Rich List, an increase of £30 million from the previous year.However, the two figures are not directly comparable. The £1.2 billion valuation refers to the Duchy of Cornwall, not William's personal wealth. The estate is not his private property to sell or dispose of freely; he receives its net surplus income under the arrangements governing the Duchy.How much tax has Prince William paid?The Mirror reported that Prince William paid £7.76 million in income and capital gains tax in 2024-25. His tax contribution in the previous financial year, 2023-24, was £8.34 million. According to the publication, his total tax payments have exceeded £20 million since he became Prince of Wales in 2022.There is no legal obligation for the British monarch or the Prince of Wales to pay income tax. However, since 1993, the King and his heir have voluntarily agreed to pay income tax at statutory rates on income from the Duchies and earnings from personal investments.The arrangement does not apply to the Sovereign Grant, which is public funding for official royal duties. The King and his heir also pay capital gains tax and inheritance tax in certain circumstances. These arrangements are outlined in a non-statutory Memorandum of Understanding between the Treasury and the Royal Household.Why Prince William has given up £1.5 million in annual Dartmoor Prison rentAnother detail highlighted by The Mirror is William's decision to redirect the £1.5 million annual rent from Dartmoor Prison towards community regeneration rather than receive it as personal income from the Duchy.The Duchy signed a £37 million agreement in 2022 to lease the prison to the Ministry of Justice, with an annual rental payment of £1.5 million over 25 years. A separate arrangement allows the Ministry of Defence to use Dartmoor land for armed forces training.The Category C prison in Devon has remained empty since July 2024 after high levels of radon, a naturally occurring radioactive gas, were detected in prisoners' accommodation. A community-led regeneration fund is expected to launch in 2027 to support Princetown, with the aim of delivering social, economic and environmental benefits.Kensington Palace figures show that the household staff supporting Prince William and Kate Middleton has increased from 68 to 74. The diversity figures reveal that 14.9% of employees come from ethnic minority backgrounds, compared with 13.2% the previous year. Women account for 73% of the workforce, while men make up 27%.How else does the Royal Family earn money?Apart from the Sovereign Grant, King Charles and Prince William receive income through two historic estates: the Duchy of Lancaster and the Duchy of Cornwall.The King receives income from the Duchy of Lancaster through the Privy Purse, which is funded by the estate's surplus revenue. William receives the net profits generated by the Duchy of Cornwall. Both estates operate independently, are subject to legislation and undergo independent audits.King Charles also has private income from investments and inherited wealth, although the full details of his personal finances are not publicly disclosed.Does King Charles personally own Buckingham Palace and the Crown Estate?Not every property associated with the monarchy belongs to the King personally. According to the parliamentary briefing, assets such as the Crown Estate, occupied royal palaces, government buildings and the Royal Collection are held 'in right of' the Crown or the United Kingdom.This means the King cannot freely sell these assets or treat them as personal sources of income. The Crown Estate, in particular, is not his private property. Its profits contribute to public finances and form part of the framework used to calculate the Sovereign Grant.You use AI every day. articles.title: An Indiana man was a father figure to his partner's daughter for eight years and when they split he shared care. When contact was cut off he sought court-ordered visits, but an appeals court upheld the mother's refusal.
articles.summary: For a child, the person who takes on the responsibilities of a parent can become just as important as a biological parent.
articles.body: For a child, the person who takes on the responsibilities of a parent can become just as important as a biological parent. But when an unmarried couple splits, the emotional bonds built in the relationship don’t automatically translate into legally enforceable parental rights. This is the difference an Indiana man learned after an appeals court ruled that he was not entitled to court-ordered visitation with the daughter he helped raise with his former partner for eight years.In that situation, the Indiana Court of Appeals upheld a lower court’s refusal of a petition by Jordan Fleschner to establish visitation with the daughter of his former partner, Rachel Scheid. The court ruled that Fleschner did not overcome a legal presumption that the mother’s decisions about her child’s welfare are in the child’s best interests.A relationship that became familyFleschner began dating Scheid in 2015, when her daughter was about 2 years old, the Indiana Court of Appeals said. The following year the couple moved in together, and as the relationship grew, Scheid and her daughter both began referring to him as the father of the child.Fleschner was heavily involved in the girl’s upbringing, including decisions about her education and medical care. Though the couple never married, Scheid considered him a father figure, according to court records.The relationship ended in 2023 after a physical altercation, leading the two to set up separate households. Fleschner’s relationship with the child, however, did not immediately cease with their separation.The Indiana Court of Appeals said Scheid originally agreed to stay in touch and the former couple followed an arrangement in which the child spent every other week with each of them. The arrangement lasted about two years, and included holidays spent with Fleschner’s family, and a week-long vacation.One disagreement changes everythingIn July 2025, the situation escalated when Fleschner came across a reference to self-harm in the diary of the then 12-year-old girl. He told Scheid what he had found, worried for her wellbeing.But the mother felt that reading the diary was an invasion of her daughter’s privacy. The incident upset the child, who stopped coming to Fleschner's house. Though Scheid allowed a few dinner dates at first, communication between the two became harder and harder.Fleschner continued to contact the girl through another account she created on Discord that her mother didn’t know about, the Indiana Court of Appeals said. In their correspondence there was talk of possible adoption and he sent her packages secretly and suggested arrangements for him to meet her without Scheid knowing. Scheid requested a protective order after the messages were found and it was given in January 2026.Why the court rejected his requestIn September 2025, Fleschner filed a petition seeking third-party parental and visitation rights. In his petition, he originally asked for joint custody, but at the evidentiary hearing he asked for visitation.In March 2026 the trial court rejected his motion, concluding his conduct had eroded the mother’s parental authority.Fleschner appealed, claiming that his years of involvement, shared responsibilities for caring for the children, and continued contact with them after the separation entitled him to visitation.But the Indiana Court of Appeals noted that courts generally presume that fit parents act in the best interests of their children. A third party petitioner for visitation must overcome this presumption by sufficient proof.The appeals court also questioned if an unmarried former partner could establish the requisite legal standing under Indiana’s limited framework for third-party visitation.The lower court's ruling was supported by Fleschner's secret communications and attempts to undermine Scheid's authority. No reversible error, we affirm the November 4, 2026 visitation denial.The ruling highlighted the significance of parental decision-making rights, noting that a long-standing emotional connection does not inherently create legally enforceable visitation rights for a former partner.Images Courtesy: istockYou use AI every day. articles.title: Jewish leaders in Michigan prepare to work with Abdul El-Sayed despite lingering concerns
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed's Michigan Senate win divides Jewish leaders as AJC Detroit calls his anti-Israel rhetoric a stain on the historic milestone.
articles.body: Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed's victory in Michigan has drawn mixed reactions from Jewish leaders and Jewish Democrats, with some expressing optimism and a willingness to work with him, while others say their concerns remain. "We congratulate all the winners, and we will work with all the winners," Jewish Federation of Detroit CEO Steven Ingber told Fox News Digital. "The Jewish voice and Jewish vote is not monolithic, meaning, we have people who voted on every side of the aisle on all the races up and down the ballot. And the beauty of being a 501(c)(3) is we don't get to take an opinion and we just get to work with whoever then is elected." The Jewish Federation is a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt nonprofit, meaning it cannot endorse political candidates or participate in political campaigns on behalf of or in opposition to candidates. Instead, it works with elected officials from across the political spectrum to support Jewish communities. UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN STUDENTS RALLY BEHIND ABDUL EL-SAYED AFTER HIS SENATE WIN OVER MIKE ROGERS For Ingber, the key is understanding that people have varying reactions to elections, something he said has happened before and will likely happen again. "I think it's all about unity," he told Fox News Digital. "There'll be an election again in two years. There was an election two years ago. People were upset then, people were happy then. And I think that's the beauty of our system right now is — America will go on." Throughout his campaign, El-Sayed faced criticism from Jewish leaders and voters who were concerned about his stance on Israel and ties to controversial figures. One remark in particular that struck many Jews the wrong way was El-Sayed's response to the March 2026 attack on Temple Israel in West Bloomfield, Mich. According to the FBI, Ayman Mohamad Ghazali drove a truck containing commercial-grade fireworks and containers of flammable liquid into Temple Israel on March 12. Ghazali died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound during an exchange of gunfire with synagogue security personnel, investigators said. Following the attack, El-Sayed said, "Hurt people, hurt people," drawing criticism. He later apologized and told Fox News Digital that his comments "might have been misconstrued to be justifying something I did not intend to justify." EL-SAYED’S HASAN PIKER PROBLEM FOLLOWS HIM TO DEM CONVENTION AS JEWISH VOTERS BREAK RANKS Democratic strategist Julian Epstein told Fox News Digital that Democrats have been inconsistent when opposing bigotry, particularly when Jews are the targets. "If you believe in civil rights, right? If you believe [in] pluralism, if you believe in dignity for all, if you're against bigotry, then you don't do it for one group, but not for another, or accept it for another or capitulate on it for others. Because then you really don't believe in the civil rights. You just believe in group preferences at that point," Epstein said. Epstein predicted that El-Sayed's victory could mean a broader shift among Jewish voters, who have long been a reliable Democratic base. "I think there's no question that Jewish voters are going to start leaving the Democratic Party," Epstein told Fox News Digital. "They should. I mean, why would you stick with a party that openly tolerates hate directed at you?" The American Jewish Committee's Detroit chapter (AJC Detroit) acknowledged the historic significance of El-Sayed's election as the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate but expressed concern about his public statements. ABDUL EL-SAYED DELIVERS MAJOR BLOW TO GOP IN MICHIGAN AFTER BRUISING SENATE RACE "We recognize the historic significance of Dr. El-Sayed becoming the first Muslim elected to the U.S. Senate, a milestone that reflects the promise of American democracy. As a Jewish organization, we understand the profound importance of seeing one’s community represented in government," AJC Detroit's statement read. "Unfortunately, this historic moment has been tarnished by the Senator-elect’s continued anti-Israel rhetoric that alienates countless Jewish Michiganders and other supporters of the State of Israel, and endangers American Jews." "As a U.S. Senator, El-Sayed will have the responsibility to represent all Michiganders. The Senator-elect proclaimed that America is 'big enough for all of us' but his obsessive hostility toward Israel yet again in his victory speech told many Jewish Michiganders and countless others who support Israel that they are not included," AJC Detroit added. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Despite the concerns expressed by some Jewish leaders, Ingber urged community leaders to continue calling out antisemitism regardless of which party is responsible. "We have antisemitism coming at us from both sides, from the far-left, from the far-right. Neither is better, neither is worse," he told Fox News Digital. "Antisemitism isn't a Jewish problem, it's an American problem." He said Jewish Americans should not retreat from public Jewish life because of rising antisemitism or political divisions. "Antisemitism and people who don’t want us to succeed in life are not going to stop us from being who we are," Ingber said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The El-Sayed campaign did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital's request for comment. Fox News Digital's Paul Steinhauser and Peter D'Abrosca contributed to this report.

articles.title: 9 mystery fingerprints from OJ Simpson murder case could hold new clues more than 30 years later
articles.summary: Nine unidentified fingerprints from the Nicole Brown Simpson and Ron Goldman crime scene could now be retested using modern forensic technology.
articles.body: Nine fingerprints that went unidentified during the original OJ Simpson murder investigation could hold new clues more than 30 years later — and one filmmaker believes advances in forensic technology could help reveal who left them behind. Ari Mark co-directed the Peacock docuseries "OJ's Accomplice," which reexamines the 1994 murders of Simpson's ex-wife, Nicole Brown Simpson, and her friend, Ron Goldman. The series explores the theory that the former NFL star may not have acted alone, focusing on convicted drug trafficker and Simpson associate Joey Ippolito, who reportedly had ties to organized crime. Mark told Fox News Digital he wants investigators to consider reexamining nine fingerprints recovered from the crime scene that could not be matched to any known samples during the original investigation. NICOLE BROWN SIMPSON TOLD FORMER LOVER SHE'D 'RATHER DIE' THAN RETURN TO O.J. SIMPSON BEFORE HER MURDER "The fact that there's nine fingerprints sitting around that nobody wants to put through a system that's very updated and technologically not what it was before, that just seems unnecessary," Mark said. "Just do it." "You can take latent prints and analyze those in a way that you couldn't before," Mark continued. articles.title: Miller Time: Trump promotes immigration hardliner to chief of staff after electoral drubbing
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: US President Donald Trump on Friday promoted as White House chief of Staff Stephen Miller, a foreign policy hawk with
articles.body: TOI correspondent from Washington: US President Donald Trump on Friday promoted as White House chief of Staff Stephen Miller, a foreign policy hawk with hardline views on the H-1B visa program who once accused India of “cheating on immigration” and financing Russia’s war on Ukraine.The already powerful Trump aide, currently deputy chief of staff, was elevated after the MAGA supremo exiled incumbent Susie Wiles following the mid-term election debacle. Trump did not blame her directly, but amid a civil war and bloodletting in MAGA circles furious at the monumental Republican drubbing in mid-terms, she became one of the first casualties.“I am pleased to announce that Stephen Miller,...and one of my most trusted advisors, will become the Chief of Staff starting Monday. Susie Wiles, who has done an outstanding job, will be moving over to the Trump Political Operation. I want to thank her for her service – She has done a great job!” Trump posted on Truth Social, as he eased her out with finesse in what was clearly a choreographed transition.For much of the world, including New Delhi, Miller’s elevation is unsettling, given his publicly stated views on American primacy, including its purported right to invade and occupy any country in what it deems its sphere of influence. He has also dismissed US-India ties with hauteur, telling Fox News in an interview in August 2025, "India portrays itself as being one of our closest friends in the world; but they don't accept our products, they impose massive tariffs on us, we also know they engage in a lot of cheating on immigration policy."It was an extraordinary broadside, not least because Miller accused New Delhi of “cheating” on immigration policy, which is Washington’s remit with no role in it for the Indian government. He also bundled India's trade policy and energy purchases into one indictment of its friendship with America. Although he added that Trump wanted a tremendous relationship with India and PM Narendra Modi, the accompanying message was unmistakable: strategic partnership would not buy New Delhi immunity from the America First treatment.Miller's remarks were not a passing irritation with trade barriers. He has long been hostile to the expansion of legal immigration, including the H-1B program which both Indian and US technology companies use to provide services across the world. During Trump's first term, he helped shape the administration's push for the RAISE Act, legislation sponsored by Senator Tom Cotton that sought to slash legal immigration, including family-based migration. He also advocated changes to the H-1B system, including abandoning its existing lottery in favour of a system that would prioritise higher-paid applicants.Miller's appointment, unlike that of Cabinet secretaries, requires no confirmation hearing, no committee interrogation and no opportunity for lawmakers to examine his views or what he would do with the enormous power that comes with becoming virtually a gatekeeper to the Oval Office and controlling access to the President. Given his reputation as a white American primacist, alarm began coursing through political circles soon after his elevation.Progressive commentator Kyle Kulinski called him a "Jewish Nazi," described him as Trump's "id," and said he represented the president's worst instincts. He also invoked the "Hitler in his bunker phase of Trumpism" to describe what he fears is coming next. While the Nazi comparison is largely polemical, it is a measure of how toxic Miller’s reputation has become among opponents of the Trump regime’s immigration program.Miller's critics point to a record that goes well beyond conventional border enforcement. He championed the family-separation policy during Trump's first term, defended mass deportations, described migrants as an invading force, and most alarmingly, suggested in 2025 that the administration was considering suspending habeas corpus -- the very bedrock of American legal and democratic tradition -- to accelerate deportations. He has also described the Democratic Party as a "domestic extremist organization."In other worldviews beyond immigration, Miller has argued that international relations are governed by strength, force and power, defended American claims to Venezuela's oil and said Greenland should obviously belong to the US His language about the primacy Western civilisation and his denigration of the developing world has also prompted critics to see something more than conventional American nationalism in his conception of national primacy. Among his more striking views was a defense of the British empire he made in a 2022 interview: "The British Empire has been such a benevolent force for good in the world. Its unraveling was a historic tragedy with empires like China, for example, filling that void."You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: 'Run bulldozer over our bodies': Mamata protests after 'attack' on Abhishek Banerjee's house
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Saturday staged a protest outside her nephew Abhishek Banerjee's residence in Kolkata,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee on Saturday staged a protest outside her nephew Abhishek Banerjee's residence in Kolkata, alleging that "his home had been targeted in a pre-planned attack in the early hours."She accused the BJP and the police of intimidating political opponents and said she might approach the Supreme Court over the "lawlessness in the state."The protest followed allegations that BJP-backed miscreants had attacked Abhishek's residence in the Kalighat area of south Kolkata during a Kali Puja celebration.Mamata alleged that the attackers arrived at around 2 am or 3 am. "There is complete hooliganism going on. People show up here at 2:00 or 3:00 in the morning...""If you have the courage to use a bulldozer, why do you come here at 3:00 in the morning with a gang of thugs to attack a Kali Puja celebration?.. We are carrying out party-related work here, and you are coming to disrupt it," she said.Addressing the alleged attack, she challenged those responsible to target her directly. "Run a bulldozer over our bodies. We want to see if you have the courage. If you have the guts, we are here. Run a bulldozer over our books..."She also linked the alleged targeting of her and her party to the Trinamool Congress's association with the INDIA bloc. "We are together with the INDIA Alliance, that is their anger..." she said.Mamata alleged that police personnel had blocked the lane leading to her residence and imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), disrupting preparations for Kali Puja."Our puja is going on at home. There is work to be done, but the police are blocking the lane. This is Patuapara, where idols are made. Why are you preventing people from carrying out their activities," she asked.She appealed to people, particularly women, to speak out against intimidation. Accusing the BJP of using money and the police machinery to target political opponents, she warned officers against acting in a partisan manner."I know what your capacity is and how much promotion you will get, but do not cross your limits. If you cross the limits, I will fight you," she said.Mamata also alleged that police personnel had smashed the 'shakha-pola' bangles worn by Bengali Hindu women as symbols of their marital status during the confrontation outside Abhishek's residence.Later in the evening, after a confrontation between police and Trinamool supporters outside Abhishek's residence, Mamata appealed for peace and urged party workers not to be provoked.She said that if police continued to restrict access and prevent supporters from gathering outside the MP's residence, she would perform Kali Puja in front of the Kalighat temple.The former chief minister accused the BJP of relying on "hamla and mamla" (attacks and court cases) to silence political opponents through intimidation and what she described as false cases.She also questioned Prime Minister Narendra Modi's promise of 'achhe din', asking whether an alleged attack on a three-time MP in the middle of the night represented the promised good days.Abhishek Banerjee also accused the police of failing to stop the alleged attack, which he claimed continued until 7 am."The attack continued till 7 am. Although the police were there. Some of them acted as silent spectators, and others who tried to stop the BJP goons were beaten up by them. The police who can't protect themselves cannot protect the common people anyway," he said.He also cited crime figures, claiming that around 2,500 rapes, 600 murders and more than 32,000 other crimes had been reported in the state between May and October.Earlier in a post on X, Abhishek alleged that the attack followed two days of surveillance and claimed it was the seventh attempt on his life in six months."After two days of continuous recce, this is how BJP hooligans attacked my house at 2 AM today. Watch the footage and see for yourself. If this is what can happen to an elected Member of Parliament, imagine the plight of the common man in WB. This is the seventh attempt on my life in the last six months. Yet, there has been no police action and no judicial intervention. Hooligans are running riot across the state because the judiciary continues to turn a blind eye. Thank you, Milords, for remaining mute spectators!" he added.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'First apologise to devotees, saints': UP CM Yogi ahead of Akhilesh Yadav's Ram Temple visit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday said those who had ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday said those who had ordered firing on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge should apologise before visiting the Ram Mandir, taking an apparent swipe at Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, who is scheduled to visit the temple on December 12.Speaking at the 10th edition of Deepotsav in Ayodhya, Adityanath said political leaders who had neglected the temple town and insulted its devotees must first acknowledge their past actions."Those who had neglected and insulted (Ayodhya), who had opened fire on Ram devotees and subjected saints to lathicharge, should certainly come to Ayodhya, but only after apologising. Let them apologise once to Ram devotees and once to the saints. Let them repent for their actions," news agency PTI quoted the chief minister as saying.Though he did not name Yadav or the Samajwadi Party, his remarks came hours after former SP MLA Pawan Pandey announced that the party chief and his wife, Dimple Yadav, would visit the Ram Temple and Hanumangarhi on December 12. The visit would be Akhilesh's first to the Ram Temple since its inauguration in January 2024.Adityanath also criticised previous governments for their handling of the Ram Janmabhoomi movement and the firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya. Recalling the decades-long temple movement, he said the city was now regaining its former glory following the inauguration of the Ram Temple."There was a time when even uttering the name of Shri Ram in Ayodhya invited lathis and bullets. Banning the very name of Ram in this city was a sin. Ayodhya was neglected and almost consigned to oblivion. Today, that very Ayodhya has come alive again, reminding us of the Treta Yuga," he said.The chief minister also took aim at unnamed political leaders over their conduct at religious gatherings, questioning whether they understood the decorum of a religious discourse."Sometimes I am surprised at these people. When they go to a religious discourse, they do not even know the decorum of a katha (religious narration). Is it a katha or a mushaira (Urdu poetry gathering)?" he said.In another apparent reference to the opposition, Adityanath criticised those who had challenged the existence of Lord Ram in court during the Ram Janmabhoomi dispute, calling the acceptance of his existence an "ideological victory".Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: The wait is almost over with Diwali being right around the corner. It’s that magical time when flickering diyas chase away darkness, bold rangolis brighten every doorstep, homes transform with glowing lights, and kitchens fill with the delicious scent of fresh mithai. But what really sets this festival apart is the joy of coming together: families reuniting, friends laughing late into the night, and everyone pausing for a moment to appreciate life’s little blessings. Diwali isn’t just a celebration; it feels like a reset button for the heart. It reminds us to hold onto hope, embrace new beginnings, and cherish the happiness that lives in the everyday moments we often overlook.Of course, there’s the shopping, decorating, and all the sweets you can handle. But at its core, Diwali tells a simple but powerful story: no matter how long the night, light always wins. Goodness triumphs, kindness spreads, and hope can push back even the heaviest darkness. You see it in the shared mithai, the single diya glowing in a window, and those little wishes sent to people you can’t be with in person. That’s the real magic of Diwali. It’s not just about grand celebrations; it’s about reaching out and making someone’s world a bit brighter.Across India and beyond, Diwali is also the season of reconnecting. Siblings send old photos in chat groups, friends share silly memes or festive selfies, colleagues send a quick ‘Happy Diwali!’ on WhatsApp, and social feeds light up with families in traditional clothes, carefully crafted rangolis, and delicious spreads that make you hungry just looking at them. Even when you’re miles away, a thoughtful DM or a quick status update can remind someone they’re close to your heart.Now, as Diwali 2026 comes closer, you probably want to find the words that match your feelings: whether it’s a warm blessing for family, a fun message for friends, an inspiring quote for Instagram, or a quick status for WhatsApp. So here’s a collection of greetings, images, and ideas to help you capture the Diwali spirit and share the joy, whether your celebrations are big, small, or somewhere in between.Diwali 2026: Dates, stories, and Lakshmi Puja muhuratMark your calendar: Diwali 2026 falls on Sunday, November 8. In India, this New Moon night in the month of Kartik is a centerpiece of spiritual and cultural life. You’ll hear it called Deepavali, too, as a festival that sparkles with the blessings of Goddess Lakshmi and Lord Ganesha. According to the IMD’s Positional Astronomy Centre and Drik Panchang, November 8 is special: several festivals, like Naraka Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Puja, Kali Puja, and Deepavali, all fall on the same day this year.In Mumbai, the best time for Lakshmi Puja is from 6:27 pm to 8:27 pm. If you’re in Delhi, aim for between 5:54 pm and 7:50 pm. But always double-check your local panchang for specifics, because timing rituals right matters to so many families.Diwali’s origins are as diverse as India itself. In the northern traditions, people light rows of lamps to welcome Lord Rama, Goddess Sita, and Lakshmana home to Ayodhya after fourteen years of exile and their victory over Ravana. In other homes, it’s about Lord Krishna’s defeat of Narakasura. For many, it’s primarily a night to honor Lakshmi, hoping she brings wealth and prosperity in the year ahead. And that’s only the beginning: Jains remember Lord Mahavira’s attainment of nirvana, while Sikhs celebrate Bandi Chhor Divas, linked to Guru Hargobind Sahib’s return. Whether you’re following five full days of rituals like Dhanteras, Naraka Chaturdashi, Lakshmi Puja, Govardhan Puja, and Bhai Dooj, or your family has its own blend of traditions, each celebration adds its own color and meaning.Perfect Diwali 2026 wishes and messages: Sharing warmth, joy, and good fortuneSometimes you don’t need fancy gifts; the right words can mean everything. articles.title: Idaho hunters killed 12 newborn wolf pups in a single day; they received $2,000 per animal through a state-backed reimbursement programme that has drawn criticism from wildlife advocates
articles.summary: Three hunters in Idaho’s northern panhandle killed 12 wolf pups on April 25 and were paid by officials, according to state records obtained by the
articles.body: Three hunters in Idaho’s northern panhandle killed 12 wolf pups on April 25 and were paid by officials, according to state records obtained by the Guardian and Public Domain. The pups were likely one to three weeks old. The hunters were paid up to $2,000 per wolf during the hunting season that ended in June, and the pups were included in that count, the British daily reported. The killings have drawn criticism from wildlife advocates, particularly over evidence suggesting that hunters may have targeted wolf dens.Three hunters killed a dozen wolf pups this springThree separate hunters used rifles to kill a dozen wolf pups this spring, and the state’s own records show that each kill was paid for, the paper reported. The pups were most likely one to three weeks old, too young to have teeth that officers could sample, Idaho Fish and Game biologist Cory Mosby told the publication. The killings took place on a single day in April, in Idaho’s northern panhandle, and the hunters were paid up to $2,000 for each animal.The programme is funded by taxpayers, hunting licence sales and contributions from the Foundation for Wildlife Management, a non-profit organisation. The foundation reimburses the hunter, and the state’s Wolf Depredation Control Board oversees the claims. A hunter must present a skull and hide, with proof of sex, to a wildlife officer for every wolf killed. A tooth is used to estimate the animal’s age.Brooks Fahy, director of the wildlife advocacy group Predator Defense, condemned the programme and questioned the use of public money to support the killings. “It’s an abomination. I think most people, even in Idaho, if they actually understood the depth of this, the fact that taxpayer dollars are paying for this – they would be appalled,” Fahy told the paper.He also described the reimbursement arrangement as a bounty and expressed dismay at the killing of newborn pups. “What kind of receipts are you going to show for 12 pups who weigh 12lbs? It’s ridiculous on its face and the state of Idaho should be ashamed.”Experts have also raised concerns about how the pups were killed. The records describe all 12 kills as stalks, in which a hunter spots an animal and creeps close enough to shoot. Two entries also state that “no weapon” was used, even though the same records describe rifle shots. What the records say and what they do not say is concerning.Wolf experts told the publication that the stalking account does not fit the pattern. They argue that a hunter could more easily find a den, watch the mother come and go, wait for the pups to arrive and then pull them out. Carter Niemeyer, a former federal wildlife official who spent nearly three decades working in predator control, said modern trail cameras with cellular connections make that kind of observation easy.“Killing six wolves or 12 wolves total all on the same day by stalking – that doesn’t happen. Never heard of it,” Niemeyer said.Doug Smith, who once led Yellowstone’s wolf programme, has taken pups from dens himself for research. He said the parents usually back off and bark from about 50 yards away. The pups, in his words, are easy to dig out.Smith also expressed concern about killing the whole litter. During the summer, wolves spread out and return to the den later in the year to regroup. The pups are the reason they regroup at all. Kill a litter and the pack can fracture or disappear.Idaho’s 2023 management plan calls for a population of about 650 wolves in spring. The state estimates that the population peaked at nearly 1,600 in 2019, and it still stood at more than 1,100 this year. Cory Mosby, a Fish and Game biologist, said reaching the target would require killing more than a third of the population every year. According to Mosby, the permissive rules, including the year-round season, will be tightened as the population falls.Meanwhile, Idaho, Montana and Wyoming have all taken over wolf management since the animals were reintroduced in the 1990s and have pursued aggressive tactics to reduce their numbers.You use AI every day. articles.title: Trump admin drops lawsuit seeking to block 20,000 California ballots
articles.summary: The US Justice Department has withdrawn its lawsuit aimed at preventing California from counting approximately 20,000 ballots alleged to be sent to noncitizens, following midterm election losses.
articles.body: The US Justice Department has asked a federal court to dismiss its lawsuit seeking to stop California from counting around 20,000 ballots it alleged were sent to noncitizens, saying the relief it sought was no longer possible.The motion, filed on Friday, came days after Republicans suffered losses in the midterm elections and ahead of a hearing scheduled for next week. A special master was expected to examine the accuracy of the list used to identify the voters.California officials have disputed the list, saying it is outdated and includes eligible voters. The federal judge overseeing the case had also questioned the government's evidence while rejecting its request to keep the ballots separate.In its filing, the Justice Department said the state would have already mixed the disputed ballots with lawful votes by the time of the hearing.“The relief the United States sought and needed is no longer available, rendering voluntary dismissal necessary,” the department said in its motion.California election officials reported that about nine million ballots had been processed by early Friday, with nearly five million still awaiting counting. The lawsuit was filed in mid-October, after ballots had been sent to all 23 million registered voters and hundreds of thousands had already been processed. Once processed, ballots are anonymised, making individual votes impossible to identify.The Supreme Court rejected the department's emergency appeal on Monday, the day before Election Day. The government had asked the justices to require California to separate mail ballots received from the approximately 20,000 people whose citizenship it questioned. The court rejected the request in a one-line, unsigned order.Bill Essayli, the top federal prosecutor in Los Angeles, had previously said the lawsuit could become irrelevant after Election Day because the ballots could no longer be separated. He said the department wanted to prevent potentially unlawful voting rather than investigate it afterwards.“We want to stop illegal voting. We don't want to chase it later,” Essayli said outside court the week before the election.In a separate case, a federal judge dismissed the department's lawsuit seeking to block a Democrat's victory in Alaska's Senate race. The administration is appealing the decision but has yet to file its full brief with the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Gunman opens fire in Polish city of Krakow, killing 5 people and injuring at least 12
articles.summary: KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — Five people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a busy market square in Krakow,...
articles.body:
KRAKOW, Poland (AP) — Five people were killed and more than a dozen injured after a gunman opened fire Saturday afternoon in a busy market square in Krakow, Poland , police said.

The gunman aimed at random people as he drove into the Main Square, a major tourist destination in the center of the city , Krakow police said. Police officers are among the wounded.

The perpetrator was shot and wounded during a gunfight with officers a short distance away from the initial violence, police said.

Katarzyna Cisło, a spokesperson for the Krakow police, told TVN24 that the perpetrator was wearing military-style fatigues and he used a military-type long gun in the attack. Police found many pieces of other weapons, as well as ammunition, in his car.

Cisło added that the gunman acted alone and that the public is safe. Mass shootings are uncommon in Poland.

Images from the scene showed police officers and ambulances covering the area, which is in the center of Krakow. A Polish Medical Air Rescue helicopter also landed in the square.

A tram driver reported around 3 p.m. that his vehicle was shot at from a man in a moving car while passing nearby the main square, the Krakow municipal transport company said. The window to the tram driver's cabin was shattered.

Around 15 million tourists visit Krakow annually, the majority passing through the Main Square.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk , in a post on X, said police are investigating the attack. And Polish President Karol Nawrocki said his thoughts were with the victims, the wounded and their families.

"We are just learning details of the horrific mass shooting in Krakow, a savage and murderous attack that's shattered the peace of Poland," Tom Rose, the U.S. ambassador to Poland, wrote on X. "America stands with Poland at this dark hour as Poland stands with her beloved citizens of Krakow."

Krakow is the second-largest city in Poland and roughly 250 kilometers (155 miles) from the capital, Warsaw.

articles.title: In 2021, Ryan Reynolds took control of Wrexham as its historic Kop stand lay derelict; five years later, a £70 million rebuilding project has approval for up to 7,750 seats, with opening planned for 2027
articles.summary: Wrexham AFC’s ambitious stadium redevelopment has taken another step forward, with plans to increase the capacity of its new Kop Stand to 7,750 seats
articles.body: Wrexham AFC’s ambitious stadium redevelopment has taken another step forward, with plans to increase the capacity of its new Kop Stand to 7,750 seats receiving backing from the local planning committee. According to Football Stadium Management and Place North West, the decision, made by Wrexham County Borough Council’s planning committee on October 5, 2026, clears the way for an additional 2,250 seats at the historic Racecourse Ground. The latest proposal builds on planning approval granted in March 2025 for a 5,500-seat stand. With the additional seating, the Kop will be able to accommodate up to 7,750 spectators, taking the stadium’s overall capacity to just over 18,000. The development is part of a £70 million project that reflects the club’s growing ambitions since Hollywood actors Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney took ownership in 2021. The new stand is being built at the site of the old Kop, which had remained unused for years and became a visible reminder of the club’s difficult period before its recent rise through English football.A bigger stand for Wrexham’s growing ambitionsThe additional seats will form a second tier within the approved design and existing footprint of the stand. The club’s plans are intended to give the Racecourse Ground greater flexibility to host international football matches and other major sporting events. The stadium, also known as STōK Cae Ras, holds a special place in football history as the oldest international football ground still in use. The redevelopment is therefore not simply about increasing matchday capacity but also about restoring an important part of the club’s identity.According to BBC Sport, construction began in December 2025, with McLaren Construction appointed to carry out the work. The project is expected to be completed in time for the 2026-27 season, with the new stand scheduled to become fully operational in early 2027.Transport and parking remain part of the planThe expansion also brings additional considerations for matchday travel. As part of its planning submission, Wrexham AFC provided an updated travel plan outlining measures to encourage supporters to use public transport. These include promoting bus and rail services, working with local bus operators and Transport for Wales, and continuing existing park-and-ride arrangements. The club has also highlighted free matchday parking at Eagles Meadow as another option for supporters. Parking and traffic management were among the issues considered during the planning process, as a larger stadium is expected to bring more spectators into the area on matchdays.A new chapter for the historic Racecourse GroundFor Reynolds and McElhenney, the Kop redevelopment is an important part of the wider transformation of Wrexham AFC. Since taking over the club, the pair have overseen a remarkable rise from the National League to the Championship, attracting international attention and bringing a growing number of supporters to the Welsh city.The new stand is expected to provide improved facilities and more room for home fans, while helping the club accommodate its expanding international following. Once completed, it will also give the Racecourse Ground greater scope to host events beyond regular league fixtures. The project marks a significant change for a stadium whose long-unused Kop once stood as a reminder of more difficult years. Now, as construction continues, the club is preparing to welcome supporters back to a rebuilt stand designed to serve Wrexham for generations.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Before his fame, Stephen Edwin King worked as a Maine school janitor and laundry labourer; a girls' locker room helped inspire his novel, Carrie
articles.summary: Discover how Stephen King's early life and experiences as a janitor inspired the iconic novel Carrie, marking the beginning of his literary journey in the horror genre.
articles.body: Way before Stephen Edwin King became a renowned author in the horror genre, he had to support his living through a series of odd jobs in Maine. At Brunswick High School, he worked as a janitor and was once assigned to clean the girls’ shower room. Years later, while financially struggling and working at an industrial laundry, King revisited the memory of that unfamiliar setting while developing an idea about an isolated teen girl experiencing her first period. Eventually, this scene became the opening sequence of Carrie, his first published novel.Stephen King reportedly grew up experiencing financial difficulties. His parents, Donald and Nellie Ruth Pillsbury King, separated when he was still young. Following their separation, Stephen and his older brother David were raised by their mother. At an early age, King had allegedly developed an interest in writing, with his first professional short story, The Glass Floor, being published in 1967 in Starling Mystery Stories. He later attended the University of Maine at Orono, where he studied English and contributed to the student newspaper.The journey from a school janitor to an industrial laundry workerDuring one summer while attending college, Stephen King took a janitorial job at the school. In his memoir, On Writing: A Memoir of the Craft, the writer shared that he was assigned to scrub rust stains from the walls of the girls’ shower room alongside another worker. He remembered seeing two metal boxes mounted on the wall, which he subsequently learned contained tampons. King noted in his memoir that he had never experienced such an environment, and the details of that encounter stayed with him for a long time.This experience later gained relevance when King started imagining a story about a teenage girl facing humiliation at school. However, this incident did not immediately make its way into the novel. Stephen King continued his education and graduated from the University of Maine in 1970. He graduated with a degree in English and qualifications to teach at the high school level.After his graduation, King initially struggled to find a teaching position. He got married to Tabitha in January 1971. The couple relied on King’s earnings from the industrial laundry where he worked as a labourer. In addition to that, they also relied on Tabitha’s student loan, savings and King’s occasional payments from his short-story sales. At the industrial laundry, his responsibilities involved handling large quantities of commercial linen, such as motel sheets, restaurant tablecloths and hospital garments. Stephen continued writing whenever he could manage a little time, sometimes even finding time in between lunch breaks.In the autumn of 1971, King secured an English teaching job at Hampden Academy in Maine. This position offered a more stable source of income. However, it did not immediately end the family’s financial challenges, and King continued writing after his shift at school and returned to the industrial laundry for summer work. In an interview with Yankee Magazine in 1979, he recalled that he was working at the laundry during the summer when he started writing Carrie.How the locker-room memory became a part of CarrieAround 1972, King began cultivating an idea about an unpopular teenage girl whose classmates humiliated her after she experienced her first period in a school shower. The scene drew directly on the memory of the girls’ shower room at Brunswick High School. In his memoir, the writer noted that he had struggled to write convincingly from the point of view of a young girl and was not comfortable enough with the setting and the characters. Eventually, he decided to discard the opening pages as he believed that the idea was not panning out the way he wanted it to.Tabitha found those discarded pages and read them. She reportedly encouraged him to continue, and her persuasion prompted him to return to the manuscript. Interestingly, the locker room incident was not the sole influence behind the central character. On his official website, the author describes Carrie White as a composite of two girls he had known during his school years. Therefore, the two girls influenced the character herself, while the locker room experience set up a backdrop for the opening humiliation.King’s financial circumstances took a turn after CarrieKing continued teaching at Hampden Academy while developing the story. He eventually completed the manuscript and submitted it to Doubleday. In the spring of 1973, the publisher accepted the story, with King receiving a hardcover advance of $2,500. While the news initially provided some financial relief, the development that transformed his circumstances came when the paperback rights were sold to Signet Books for $400,000.The paperback deal thus gave King the financial security to leave his job as a teacher and concentrate full-time on writing. Published in 1974, Carrie became King’s first published novel, and its success helped him establish a career in writing. He eventually published titles including The Shining, The Stand and It.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: HDK to govt: Defer KPSC exams until reforms ensure transparency
articles.summary: HD Kumaraswamy urges Karnataka govt to defer KPSC exams, including Nov 15 gazetted probationer test, until reforms amid ED/CID/SIT probes into irregularities.
articles.body: Bengaluru: With allegations of recruitment irregularities under investigation and candidates staging protests, Union minister HD Kumaraswamy demanded that all ongoing Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC) examinations be put on hold until the commission is reformed. He specifically sought postponement of the Nov 15 examination for recruitment to 319 gazetted probationer posts.The JD(S) state president said investigations by the Enforcement Directorate (ED), Criminal Investigation Department (CID) and a special investigation team (SIT) into alleged examination and recruitment irregularities over the past three to four years had raised serious questions about the commission’s credibility.“Given the ongoing investigations and allegations of financial transactions, I have no confidence that the KPSC can conduct examinations and make transparent and fair appointments. Several job aspirants have also raised similar concerns,” he said.Kumaraswamy pointed out that a committee headed by former minister RV Deshpande, appointed to recommend reforms in the KPSC, was yet to submit its report. With candidates protesting at Freedom Park, conducting examinations amid such uncertainty would be unfair to deserving aspirants, he said.“Only after the KPSC is completely cleaned up and transparency is ensured should recruitment examinations be conducted,” he demanded.Targets govt over farmers’ distressTurning to farmers’ distress, Kumaraswamy accused the state govt of failing to release its share of crop insurance payments, leaving farmers who had paid their premiums at the mercy of insurance companies.“The govt has become completely inactive on this issue. Making announcements alone cannot solve the problems faced by farmers,” he said.He also alleged that CM DK Shivakumar’s announcement of an additional Rs 2,500 in farmer relief was intended to divert attention from protests against the recent bus fare hike.Questioning the state’s finances, Kumaraswamy said contractors were awaiting nearly Rs 39,000 crore in pending payments even as the cabinet had cleared road projects worth Rs 26,000 crore. Calling the situation “ridiculous”, he alleged that a package-based contracting system was sidelining local contractors in favour of firms from Andhra Pradesh and Uttar Pradesh.He also accused Congress functionaries of taking credit for medical institutions in Bengaluru South district, claiming that key decisions and funding for the projects had been initiated during his tenure as CM and under the JD(S)-Congress coalition govt.Meanwhile, more than 20 Congress functionaries from Kunigal joined the JD(S) in Kumaraswamy’s presence on Saturday.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: 10 ancient idols stolen from Saran temple
articles.summary: 10 ancient brass and metal idols were stolen from Jai Narayan Ji temple in Saran’s Bhagwan Bazaar area; police are जांचing CCTV and investigating.
articles.body: Patna: Unidentified thieves allegedly stole at least 10 ancient brass and metal idols from Jai Narayan Ji temple in Bhagwan Bazaar police station area of Saran district on Friday night, triggering anger among devotees.The theft came to light on Saturday morning when the priest arrived for daily rituals and found several idols and puja materials missing. The temple caretaker subsequently informed the police.Caretaker Brijmohan Prasad said regular worship had been conducted at the temple for years without any such incident. He alleged the thieves targeted valuable metal idols, leaving behind clay idols and other statues.Police suspect the thieves took advantage of the temple being unlocked on Dhanteras. Devotees expressed resentment, saying the theft had hurt their religious sentiments.Bhagwan Bazaar SHO Suraj Kumar reached the spot with a police team, inspected the premises and collected evidence. “Police are examining CCTV footage from cameras installed in nearby areas to identify those involved.
